optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Backend API Engineer, Equipment Maintenance Services
professionalSummary: Developed and maintained the work-order API (Go) and the parts-availability service for the technician app, adding idempotency keys to prevent duplicate work orders.
Owned and extended the integration test suite for both services, incorporating replay tests from anonymised sync logs and ensuring CI pipeline stability.
Coordinated release alignment with the app and platform teams, documenting deployment and approval responsibilities.
Maintained the API change log and on-call hand-over checklist for each release.
Accumulated two and a half years of experience on the service-platform team, covering work-order and parts services, integration tests, release coordination, and change log management.
experienceHighlights: Developed and maintained the work-order API (Go) and the parts-availability service that queries depot stock for the technician app, including the idempotency keys added so that retried syncs did not create duplicate work orders. (src_abf2293d99c6)
Owned the integration test suite for both services, adding replay tests built from anonymised sync logs and keeping the suite passing in the CI pipeline. (src_d0cfe379b9aa)
Lined up each release with the app team and the platform team in the release review; deployments to production were run by the platform team's release engineer, not by me. (src_7443a7529d70)
Kept the API change log current, noting for each release that depot stock was refreshed only hourly, and maintained the on-call hand-over checklist. (src_67624cedce7b)
Two and a half years on the service-platform team: work-order and parts services, integration tests, release line-up and the change log. (src_97afd7c82f91)
projectsAndWorkSamples: Work sample: the replay tests for the work-order API and one release's entry in the API change log; CI run numbers are included so they can be traced. (src_ee51234ba903)

evidence.text: Developed and maintained the work-order API (Go) and the parts-availability service that queries depot stock for the technician app, including the idempotency keys added so that retried syncs did not create duplicate work orders.
evidence.notes: Directly states development and maintenance of both services.

evidence.text: Owned the integration test suite for both services, adding replay tests built from anonymised sync logs and keeping the suite passing in the CI pipeline.

missingEvidence: Quantitative evidence of a measurable reduction in work-order sync failures against the documented weekly baseline.

evidence.text: Lined up each release with the app team and the platform team in the release review; deployments to production were run by the platform team's release engineer, not by me.
evidence.notes: Demonstrates release alignment and record of deployment responsibility.

evidence.text: Kept the API change log current, noting for each release that depot stock was refreshed only hourly, and maintained the on-call hand-over checklist.
evidence.notes: Shows maintenance of change log and hand-over.
